question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 3.
solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. 'for long'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look into the statement in detail: 
 
• "For long" correctly completes the sentence and makes grammatical sense.
 
• The phrase "for long" effectively conveys that the droplets do not remain suspended in the air for an extended period.
 
• In English, we commonly use "for long" to describe something that does not last a long time, which fits the context of the sentence perfectly.
 
 
• ​The complete passage is: *The coronavirus (1) spreads mostly through droplets that people send (2) out when they talk, sneeze, or cough. These usually don't stay in the air (3) for long and they don't go farther than six feet. But the coronavirus might also travel (4) through tiny aerosol particles that can linger in the air for up to three hours and travel farther away. You might also catch the coronavirus if you touch something an infected person (5) has touched and then touch your eyes, nose, or mouth.*​
